findings.where: i5.body.final.html, paintLife: the amber 'the rule expects' curve (const curve = A(G.over, ...), set from B.relax near line 696), steps 3-12 and the bathtub
findings.what: The amber curve is drawn in the over layer, so once it relaxes it runs straight through the top bead of every year's column that holds more than the rule expects: 4 beads in the 5-year picture (years 0, 2, 3 and 4), 7 at the MTBF, 10 for pairs in series at 10 years and 12 on the bathtub; that breaks 'the bell never runs through a bead', so draw it in the under layer as the swarm's bell is, and let the taller columns sit over it.

findings.where: the whole lesson: lay() and B.stack for every life view; the colour key stays hidden
findings.what: Nothing visible changed in the restyle: the failed units still stack as the old year-column pile, with no swarm, fade or key, which is what the guide says for lifetimes but makes this the one lesson where Dan sees none of the swarm he chose; if he wants it here too, the failed units could settle as a centred swarm at their own lifetimes along the years axis, with the rule's curve as its mirrored outline under the beads.

findings.where: i5.body.final.html, nowLine and mtbfLine (lines 676 and 681) against the pile columns (SCL 9.73 wide, bead r 4.32)
findings.what: The clock's hand (1.4 wide) and the dashed MTBF line (1.6 wide) stand on a year boundary where neighbouring columns are only 1.1 units apart, so at rest each one tucks behind the beads on either side and looks as if it touches them, for example the hand at 5 years against the year-4 column at 360 px; slightly smaller beads, about r 3.9, would give both lines clear air.

findings.where: i5.body.final.html, Pairs in parallel and Two chargers: harnessOut (w + 4.6 = 13.2 wide) and harnessIn (w + 2.2 = 10.8) on pairs 11 units apart
findings.what: Neighbouring harness outlines overlap and the inner fills leave only a 0.16-unit seam between them, so the 25 harnesses likely read as one long band rather than one per pair, which is the opposite of what the build log says; a thinner outline, about 10.4 wide, or pairs spaced further apart would give each pair its own wall.
